MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "what do you ask a spine patient?"
- "Pain, paraesthesia, weakness, deformity, and bladder or bowel trouble."
- "Then claudication distance, red flags, and the effect on work and daily life."
- "Never accept 'mechanical back pain' outside 20–55 years without investigation."

### Pain — where, how, when
| Ask | Answer points to |
|---|---|
| Site | neck (cervical); low back pain, LBP (lumbar) |
| Referred to | neck: scapula, arm · back: buttock, leg |
| Character | dull aching → degeneration, stenosis · sharp radiating → disc |
| Onset | sudden → disc · insidious → infection, tumour · gradual → stenosis |
| Time | after activity → mechanical · at night → infection or tumour |

#### Radicular or referred pain?
| | Radicular | Referred |
|---|---|---|
| Tingling, numbness | yes | no |
| Distribution | follows a dermatome | does not |
| Below the knee | may reach the toes | does not cross the knee |
| Motor loss | may occur | no |

- Sciatica = pain only; radiculopathy = pain plus motor or sensory loss
- **Memory:** radicular pain crosses the knee; referred pain stops at it

### Weakness, myelopathy, cauda equina
| Complaint | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Weakness, cervical | lower motor neuron at the level, upper below |
| Weakness, lumbar | lower motor neuron, or cauda equina |
| Clumsy hands, unsteady gait | cervical myelopathy |
| Saddle numbness, bladder or bowel loss | cauda equina syndrome (large central L4–5 disc) |

- **Memory:** cauda equina = **SMSR** — saddle, motor, sphincter, reflex (Nagah)
- Neurogenic bladder = painless overflow, not prostate or stress leak

### Claudication — neurogenic or vascular?
| | Neurogenic (spinal stenosis) | Vascular |
|---|---|---|
| Back pain | yes | no |
| Leg pain | buttock to calf, both legs | calf, one leg |
| Relief | sitting or bending forward | standing still |
| Uphill, bicycle | easier | worse |
| Pulses | intact | weak or absent |

- **Memory:** neurogenic loves the shopping trolley; vascular stops and stands

### Red flags
| Red flag | Think of |
|---|---|
| First back pain at 55 or older; or very young | tumour, infection |
| Weight loss, past cancer | metastasis |
| Night pain, fever | infection or tumour |
| Fast progressive neurological deficit | cord or cauda compression |
| Bladder or bowel incontinence | cauda equina |

- **Memory:** age, cancer, fever, night pain, neurology, bladder — any one → image now

### Deformity history (scoliosis, kyphosis)
- Use the patient's words (high shoulder, hump), never "scoliosis"

| Ask | Why |
|---|---|
| Pregnancy, delivery, milestones | neuromuscular or syndromic cause |
| Menarche | progression risk is highest about a year after it |
| Pain | scoliosis plus back pain → exclude spondylolysis |

| Nerves | numbness, weakness, gait, hand clumsiness |
| Sphincters | bladder, bowel, saddle numbness |

- "Standing: look, feel, move, Schober, Adam's; then walk, heels and toes."
- "Sitting: rotation, the neck, upper limb neurology. Supine: lower limb neurology, SLR."
- "Prone: femoral stretch. Finish with hips, SIJ, pulses and perianal sensation."

### The route on one page
| Position | What you do (in order) |
|---|---|
| Standing | Look: front, side, behind · Feel: spines, step, spasm |
| Standing | Move: flex, extend, bend · Special: Schober, Adam's, Kemp, Romberg |
| Walking | gait · heels, toes, one leg, squat |
| Sitting | curve corrected? · lumbar rotation · the neck |
| Sitting | Neuro: arm roots, cervical tests, knee and ankle jerks |
| Supine | Neuro: leg roots, Babinski, clonus · SLR group · SIJ tests |
| Prone | femoral stretch |
| Finish | hips, SIJ, pulses, abdomen, perianal sensation |

- **Memory:** stand, walk, sit, lie, turn — Look, Feel, Move, Special in each

### Standing
#### Expose and look
- Expose to the underwear, barefoot; chaperone and permission for a woman

| View | Look for |
|---|---|
| Front | head over pelvis, shoulder level, pelvic tilt |
| Side | lordosis, kyphosis, hip and knee flexion |
| Behind | scars, skin marks, list, scoliosis, waist |

- Café-au-lait spots → count them: neurofibromatosis
- Sacral hair tuft or dimple → spina bifida
- Plumb line from C7 falls on mid-sacrum

#### Sagittal profile
| Finding | Causes |
|---|---|
| Regular kyphosis | senile, osteoporotic, Scheuermann, ankylosing spondylitis (AS) |
| Angular kyphosis (gibbus) | TB, trauma, congenital, tumour |
| More lordosis | hip FFD, thoracic kyphosis, spondylolisthesis |
| Less lordosis | disc spasm, flat back after surgery |

- Kyphosis counts as increased above 45° (Kasr Al-Ainy)

| Landmark | Level |

| First spinous process felt | C2 |

9.03.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you examine the neurology?"
- "Explain, expose, compare sides. Tone, power, sensation, reflexes — root by root."
- "Then upper motor neuron signs: Hoffmann, Babinski, clonus. Then perianal sensation."

### Rules
| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| Explain each test first | misunderstood orders give grade 3 instead of 5 |
| Stabilise above the joint | stops trick movements |
| Compare with the other side | the other side is the normal |
| Grade, do not describe | "MRC grade 4", not "weak" |

### Sensation
| Modality | Test with |
|---|---|
| Pain | pinprick |
| Light touch | cotton tip |
| Vibration | tuning fork on bone |
| Joint position | big toe or finger, eyes closed |

- Grade 2 = normal, 1 = impaired, 0 = lost

[[FIG: Fig 9.13 — Dermatome map · 9.03

### Power
- MRC grades → ch 1 (1.4); start with resistance, then gravity, then gravity eliminated

### Upper limb roots
| Root | Motor | Reflex | Sensation |
|---|---|---|---|
| C5 | deltoid, biceps | biceps | badge area to the elbow |
| C6 | biceps, wrist extensors | brachioradialis | lateral forearm, thumb, index |
| C7 | triceps, wrist flexors, finger extensors | triceps | middle finger |
| C8 | finger flexors | none | ring and little fingers |
| T1 | interossei (spread the fingers) | none | medial elbow |

- C8 = finger **flexors**, not extensors (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- T2 axilla, T4 nipple, T10 umbilicus
- **Memory:** reflexes 5-6-7 — biceps, brachioradialis, triceps

### Is a cervical root compressed?
- **Memory:** close the hole → pain (Spurling); open the hole → relief (distraction, hand on head)

#### Spurling test
- **Aim:** cervical root compression
- **How:** patient sitting looks to the painful side; you extend, press on the vertex
- **Positive:** arm pain below the elbow → root compression
- **Why:** extension and rotation narrow the foramen
